thread:
olivia: Heads-up — noticed a weird spike pattern on the GPU heatmap in us-west-2 over the last ~2h. Temps jump+drop every ~10m on a subset of cards, but errors don't always line up. digging now.
martin: can you link the dashboard? which panel? :mag:
olivia: infra/gpu/heatmap -> 'temp_noise_by_card' panel. here's a quick snapshot link: https://grafana/redwood/d/GPUs/heatmap?orgId=1
sre-bot: Alert triggered: GPU_TEMPERATURE_NOISE_USW2 (firing) — 8 cards above noise threshold (>3 sigma) in last 15m. Rule: `increase in temp stddev` -> routed to #eng-runtime and @oncall. :rotating_light:
nadeem: I saw similar last month when kernel driver jittered on a few A100 hosts. Could be firmware/driver flakiness causing telemetry gaps, not actual thermal issue. Can we correlate with `nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total` and `card_reset_count`?
olivia: good call. ran a quick query:

```
sum by (card) (rate(nvidia_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m]))
```
only 2 of the 8 noisy cards show ECC spikes, but 6/8 have small xid bursts (0.1-0.5/min)
elaine: I'd rather avoid immediate replacement. Proposal: add a composite signal that weights (xid_rate * card_age_factor) + temp_noise_score, and only escalate to hardware-replacement when composite > 5 for > 30m. This avoids churn on young cards with transient xid bursts.
martin: agree on composite. also want to route noisy-but-low-composite to a "soft-drain" pool so workloads can be shifted for 24-48h while we observe. frees capacity without full RMA cost.
olivia: action items: 1) update gpu heatmap to include `composite_risk` column, 2) new alert rule: fire P2 if composite >5 for 30m, P3 if composite >3 for 15m, 3) add soft-drain runbook and autoscaler hook to move pods.
oncall-bot: @oncall assigned: nadeem. ETA 30m for triage.
nadeem: working through logs. early signal: bunch of `nvidia-mig` reconfig logs around 08:12 and a libnvidia change at 08:10 on two hosts. pulling kernel and driver versions now.
elaine: Dashboard design notes (for the panel):
- Left: heatmap (temp noise) by card, stack by pod namespace
- Middle: timeseries of `xid_rate`, `ecc_rate`, `card_reset_count` (5m rate)
- Right: table with `card_age_days`, `composite_risk`, `current_pool` and `last_reboot`
- Add small sparkline row for 24h trend and a color-coded `noise_snr` (signal-to-noise ratio)
martin: alert expr suggestion (PromQL-ish):
```
avg_over_time((xid_rate*age_factor + temp_stddev)[30m:1m]) > 5
```
and route to #infra-fallback when >8 but still below replacement threshold.
olivia: cost note — replacing a single A100 equivalent instead of soft-draining ~10 hosts impacts capex vs lost throughput. we should add a cost-estimate column in the runbook: expected lost qps and replacement spend.
nadeem: triage update: two cards have repeated `xid` with PCIe link flaps in dmesg. recommending soft-drain + vendor ticket rather than immediate RMA for now. will run extended soak.
elaine: I'll open a Grafana PR with the panel layout and example queries. tagging @dash-team for review.
martin: can we also add a small metric for "allocation_failures_due_to_card_unavailable" so we can quantify user impact when we soft-drain pools? helps with SLO reasoning.
olivia: yes — add `gpu_alloc_reject_count{reason="card_unavailable"}` to the dashboard and wire to the SLO dashboard. If soft-drain causes >1% increase in 1h, escalate to P1 and consider temporary capacity burst.
oncall-bot: update: oncall nadeem acknowledged. next update in 45m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
olivia: thanks y'all. keeping this thread as single source. will link PR + runbook once ready. :thumbsup:
